Tigecycline versus imipenem/cilastatin for complicated intra-abdominal infection: clinical cure at test-of-cure

Among trials randomising adults with complicated intra-abdominal infection to tigecycline or to imipenem/cilastatin, how does the proportion cured at the test-of-cure visit compare, and does that comparison survive the choices made in reaching it?

What this object claims to contain

Every trial found that randomises this population to this intervention against this comparator and publishes per-arm counts in the analysis population is held and pooled. One further eligible registrational trial exists whose per-arm figures are published only inside a pooled report this build could not open; it is listed as eligible and contributing no data, and it is not excluded. Trials in the other licensed indication, and cIAI trials against a different comparator, are outside the scope and are named where they are excluded rather than left unmentioned.

Not held in this object. No search record is held in this object. The included set was reconciled against published syntheses rather than produced by a database search, so no query, date or yield can be shown. Treat the included set as a convenience sample, not a systematic one.
Not held in this object. No screening log is recorded for this review. The included set was reconciled against published syntheses rather than screened from a search, so no records-identified, excluded-with-reason or dual-screening counts exist.

Pooled result

RR 0.9351 (0.8885 to 0.9842), 95% interval

Clinical cure at the test-of-cure visit. random, estimator REML, k = 3.

τ² 0.000025 · I² 7.287% · Q 2.157 on 2 df

Favours: imipenem/cilastatin (higher is better) — The pooled interval lies wholly below the null and the outcome is beneficial, so the comparator is the arm favoured. This is the reading an earlier presentation of this review inverted.

tau-squared and I-squared are recorded beside this line, on the measure actually used. They are not the grounds on which that measure was chosen.

Identical across the pooled trials: indication, comparator, outcome definition and analysis population. Not identical, and pooled anyway with the reason recorded against each: blinding, region and trial size. Each difference that could plausibly drive the result has a matching entry in the sensitivity block.

The analysis population is part of the estimand and this pool crosses it. Read from the registrations on 2026-08-21: NCT00081744 registers 'no primary outcome is recorded on this registration' (population: None recorded); NCT00136201 registers 'Clinical response for all microbiologically evaluable and microbiologically modified intent-to-treat subjects' (population: ME and m-mITT); NCT01721408 registers 'Clinical Response at the Test-of-Cure (TOC) Assessment Within the Clinically Evaluable (CE) Population' (population: CE). The populations pooled are CE and ME and m-mITT.

A clinically evaluable population excludes protocol violators and indeterminate responses, and microbiologically-defined populations exclude patients without a qualifying pathogen. Those are selected subsets of the modified intent-to-treat population and systematically yield higher cure rates. A cure-rate ratio computed in one is not an estimate of the same quantity as one computed in another, so this pooled value depends on which trial registered which population.

Not that the arithmetic is wrong. Not that the direction would reverse -- that would need the per-population counts and is not established. And not that these are non-inferiority trials: The registrations fetched do not use that word, so the design question is unresolved from the registry rather than assumed.

A published network meta-analysis of fifteen studies and 6,745 participants concludes: 'No differences in clinical and microbiological outcomes were observed between different carbapenems and TGC' (Yu et al., Medicine 2019, PMID 31577763). This pool reports RR 0.9351 (0.8885 to 0.9842) on three trials -- an interval that excludes no difference, read as tigecycline being inferior on clinical cure.

The inferiority conclusion does not survive this object's own adjustment. The Hartung-Knapp interval at k = 3 is 0.8327 to 1.0501 on t = 4.3027 with 2 degrees of freedom, and it includes no difference. A reader taking inferiority from this page is reading the unadjusted interval only.

One contributing trial is OPEN-LABEL (NCT00136201 registers masking none) on an assessed clinical-response endpoint; one registers no primary outcome at all (NCT00081744, open item O0a) so its result cannot be checked against anything; and the three define their primary in different analysis populations. GRADE certainty is very LOW.

Which twelve studies the network carries that this object does not. The abstract names none and no included-study table was read, so the gap is counted and not identified.

Read this before the interval above. The estimate is 0.9351 (0.8885 to 0.9842), which excludes no difference and reads as tigecycline being inferior on clinical cure. This project's own hartung-knapp interval at k = 3 IS 0.8327 to 1.0501, on a t critical value of 4.3027 with 2 degrees of freedom, and it includes no difference. The house rule already requires the adjusted interval to be shown beside the unadjusted one where k is small, because that is the honest width; on this pool the two disagree about the conclusion.

Yu et al., Medicine 2019, PMID 31577763, a Bayesian network meta-analysis of fifteen studies and 6,745 participants, concluded: 'No differences in clinical and microbiological outcomes were observed between different carbapenems and TGC.' the adjusted interval and the larger literature agree with each other and not with the unadjusted reading.

The stored estimate is not changed. Withdrawing or restating a published number is a content decision. What has been done is to put the adjusted interval and the disagreement where a reader meets the number, because a page that concludes more than its own stated method supports had been passing while pages that refuse honestly are marked incomplete.

Read this beside the estimate. This review pools cure rates for tigecycline in complicated intra-abdominal infection and says nothing, anywhere, about all-cause mortality. Tigecycline carries an FDA boxed warning for increased all-cause mortality, and complicated intra-abdominal infection is among the indications it was drawn from. Independently of the label, one of the three pooled registrations posts an asymmetry of its own: NCT01721408 reports serious adverse events in 32 of 232 on tigecycline against 16 of 232 on imipenem/cilastatin, read from its own posted results. A cure-rate estimate for this drug, in this indication, presented without that, is the smaller half of the story.

A cross-lane check reported that this pool carries three of four trials and that the omitted one is the only one favouring the drug. The fourth registration is NCT00230971, and its comparator is ceftriaxone plus metronidazole, not imipenem/cilastatin. Adding it would combine two comparators in one estimate. The exclusion stands; it is now recorded, which it was not before.

This object's own sensitivity analyses are the place to read this estimate against. Changing the summary statistic to an odds ratio gives 0.4987 (0.1955 to 1.2722) and reversing which category counts as the event gives 1.8683 (0.7784 to 4.4844) -- both include no difference. An inferiority reading taken from 0.9351 (0.8885 to 0.9842) does not survive this object's own robustness checks, and that is recorded here rather than left for a reader to assemble.

An earlier version declared this identical with nothing behind it, which a build-time rule added after the malaria comparator defect now refuses.
blindingdifferstwo trials are double-blind and one is open-label. An open-label trial of a subjective, investigator-assessed outcome is the more susceptible to assessment bias, and its removal is one of the leave-one-out analyses
test of cure windowdifferseach protocol defines its own test-of-cure interval and the three do not coincide: one runs fourteen to thirty-five days after therapy, one twelve to thirty-seven, and one fourteen to twenty-one days after the last dose. Section 3.2.4 is what permits this and what it asks for: it says a review commonly specifies a time frame rather than a specific time point precisely to handle diversity in timing across studies, and its expectation on predefining time points asks that no more than one time point be taken from each study for an outcome, which is what happens here. An earlier version of this table called the outcome identical without qualification, which made the windows look the same; a reviewer read the three protocols and found they are not
regiondiffersone trial is multinational and two enrolled in one country
trial sizediffersthe evaluable populations differ by roughly an order of magnitude between the largest and the smallest, so the smallest contributes little weight but can still move a random-effects estimate

The methods rule governing this decision

Decision: Pool the three trials that share indication, comparator, outcome and analysis population, on the risk ratio of cure, by random effects; and report in the same breath that the exclusion of the null does not survive the alternatives the Handbook asks to be tested

Cochrane Handbook sections: 3.2.4, 10.4.3, 10.10.1, 10.10.2, 10.10.4, 10.14

Section 10.4.3 recommends that meta-analyses be undertaken using risk ratios or odds ratios and asks for a sensible, declared choice of which category is the event; the risk ratio of cure is used and the event category is declared on the outcome. That section also warns that selecting an effect measure because it is the most consistent is not a recommended strategy, since it can spuriously maximise precision, and this object is bound by that warning: the risk ratio is not chosen for its lower inconsistency, it is chosen as one of the two measures the section recommends and on its ease of interpretation, which the same section discusses. The odds ratio is reported beside it. What the pooled trials differ in is recorded under 10.10.1 rather than treated as disqualifying, and the inconsistency statistic is reported in the bands of 10.10.2. Section 10.14, with 10.4.3's own instruction to test the choice of statistic and of event category, is why the sensitivity block exists and why its result is reported as prominently as the primary line. Section 10.10.4 is what governs the model and the estimator, which the effect-measure sections do not: it records that estimators other than DerSimonian and Laird perform better and that restricted maximum likelihood is now the default in the Cochrane software, and its subsection on few studies advises comparing the methods when there are only two or three. That comparison is in the sensitivity block, on all three estimators and on both interval methods.

Is the finding robust to how it was reached?

Section 10.4.3 says in terms that it may be wise to test whether the choice of summary statistic and of which category counts as the event is critical to the conclusions, and section 10.14 is the general authority for testing arbitrary or unclear decisions. Here the answer is that it IS critical, and that is the most important thing this object has to report.

Table 9. Is the finding robust to how it was reached?
What was changedRR or its alternative (95% CI)I²Effect on the conclusion
the summary statistic, from risk ratio to odds ratio0.4987 (0.1955 to 1.272)58.76%the interval now includes the null
which category counts as the event, from cure to its complement, treatment failure1.868 (0.7784 to 4.484)59.73%the interval now includes the null
the model, from random effects to fixed effect0.9352 (0.8888 to 0.9839)7.287%unchanged in substance
the analysis population, to each trial's best-available modified intention-to-treat population, across all three trials. Two supply a MICROBIOLOGICAL one and the third a PLAIN one, so this row deliberately crosses a definition difference that the row below refuses to cross0.9304 (0.8821 to 0.9812)0%still excludes the null
the analysis population, from microbiologically evaluable to microbiological modified intention-to-treat, across the two trials that publish that SAME definition0.9281 (0.8601 to 1.001)0%the interval now includes the null, on the two trials that permit the comparison
the study set, by removing study-3010.9107 (0.8542 to 0.971)0%still excludes the null

the study set, by removing study-b18111850.9373 (0.8495 to 1.034)49.13%the interval now includes the null

The direction is stable: every trial's point estimate, every alternative statistic and every leave-one-out set puts tigecycline below its comparator on cure. What is not stable is the exclusion of the null. It survives only under the risk ratio of cure, on the evaluable population, with all three trials in. Reporting the primary line without this block would present a fragile result as a firm one.

Does the answer depend on the pooling method?

Section 10.10.4.4 records that other estimators of the between-study variance perform better than DerSimonian and Laird and that the restricted maximum likelihood method is now the default in the Cochrane software, and section 10.10.4.5 advises in terms that with only two or three studies the different methods should be compared in a sensitivity analysis. This pool has three, so the comparison is done rather than the advice merely cited.

Table 10. Does the answer depend on the pooling method?
Between-study varianceIntervalSummary (95% CI)τ²
DerSimonian-Laird (DL)ordinary (Wald)0.9348 (0.8865 to 0.9858)0.000166
Paule-Mandel (PM)ordinary (Wald)0.9348 (0.8864 to 0.9859)0.000178
restricted maximum likelihood (REML)ordinary (Wald)0.9351 (0.8885 to 0.9842)0.000025
restricted maximum likelihood (REML)Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman (HKSJ)0.9351 (0.8327 to 1.05)0.000025

The three variance estimators agree closely, which is what the Handbook reports is usual: they can differ substantially in the heterogeneity they estimate but seldom move the summary effect much. The interval method is what matters here. Under the Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman interval the null is no longer excluded, and section 10.10.4.5 says exactly what to make of that: with three studies that interval is likely to be too wide, while the ordinary one is likely to be too narrow, so neither is taken as decisive and both are shown.

The headline estimator is restricted maximum likelihood, which is what section 10.10.4.4 records as the default in the Cochrane software and the direction its evidence points: it says in terms that other methods for estimating the between-study variance perform better than DerSimonian and Laird. An earlier version of this object kept DerSimonian and Laird as the headline and gave as its reason that the local validator could recompute it. A reviewer was right that this is not a methodological reason at all, and that it mattered here, because the headline is the line that excludes the null. The tooling was the thing that had to move, not the method: the validator now recomputes restricted maximum likelihood independently, so the Handbook's default and external checkability are no longer in tension. DerSimonian and Laird is still shown beside it, and it makes almost no difference to the summary, which is what the Handbook says to expect.

Other recorded qualifications

Statements this review records about the limits of what it establishes, which are not shown elsewhere on this page. They are reproduced from the object verbatim and are not summarised.

Table 13. Other recorded qualifications
Analysed scopethe microbiologically evaluable participants assessed at the test-of-cure visit. This is an evaluable population, not the randomised one.
A this pool crosses analysis populationsThe analysis population is part of the estimand and this pool crosses it. Read from the registrations on 2026-08-21: NCT00081744 registers 'no primary outcome is recorded on this registration' (population: None recorded); NCT00136201 registers 'Clinical response for all microbiologically evaluable and microbiologically modified intent-to-treat subjects' (population: ME and m-mITT); NCT01721408 registers 'Clinical Response at the Test-of-Cure (TOC) Assessment Within the Clinically Evaluable (CE) Population' (population: CE). The populations pooled are CE and ME and m-mITT.
C what is not claimedNot that the arithmetic is wrong. Not that the direction would reverse -- that would need the per-population counts and is not established. And not that these are non-inferiority trials: The registrations fetched do not use that word, so the design question is unresolved from the registry rather than assumed.
A a fifteen study network finds no difference where this pool finds inferiorityA published network meta-analysis of fifteen studies and 6,745 participants concludes: 'No differences in clinical and microbiological outcomes were observed between different carbapenems and TGC' (Yu et al., Medicine 2019, PMID 31577763). This pool reports RR 0.9351 (0.8885 to 0.9842) on three trials -- an interval that excludes no difference, read as tigecycline being inferior on clinical cure.
B and our own small sample correction agrees with themThe inferiority conclusion does not survive this object's own adjustment. The Hartung-Knapp interval at k = 3 is 0.8327 to 1.0501 on t = 4.3027 with 2 degrees of freedom, and it includes no difference. A reader taking inferiority from this page is reading the unadjusted interval only.
C the evidence base here is weaker than the interval suggestsOne contributing trial is OPEN-LABEL (NCT00136201 registers masking none) on an assessed clinical-response endpoint; one registers no primary outcome at all (NCT00081744, open item O0a) so its result cannot be checked against anything; and the three define their primary in different analysis populations. GRADE certainty is very LOW.
D what is not establishedWhich twelve studies the network carries that this object does not. The abstract names none and no included-study table was read, so the gap is counted and not identified.
E the inferiority reading does not survive this project s own adjustmentRead this before the interval above. The estimate is 0.9351 (0.8885 to 0.9842), which excludes no difference and reads as tigecycline being inferior on clinical cure. This project's own hartung-knapp interval at k = 3 IS 0.8327 to 1.0501, on a t critical value of 4.3027 with 2 degrees of freedom, and it includes no difference. The house rule already requires the adjusted interval to be shown beside the unadjusted one where k is small, because that is the honest width; on this pool the two disagree about the conclusion.
F and a fifteen study network reached the same conclusion as the adjusted intervalYu et al., Medicine 2019, PMID 31577763, a Bayesian network meta-analysis of fifteen studies and 6,745 participants, concluded: 'No differences in clinical and microbiological outcomes were observed between different carbapenems and TGC.' the adjusted interval and the larger literature agree with each other and not with the unadjusted reading.
A this page never mentions the mortality warningRead this beside the estimate. This review pools cure rates for tigecycline in complicated intra-abdominal infection and says nothing, anywhere, about all-cause mortality. Tigecycline carries an FDA boxed warning for increased all-cause mortality, and complicated intra-abdominal infection is among the indications it was drawn from. Independently of the label, one of the three pooled registrations posts an asymmetry of its own: NCT01721408 reports serious adverse events in 32 of 232 on tigecycline against 16 of 232 on imipenem/cilastatin, read from its own posted results. A cure-rate estimate for this drug, in this indication, presented without that, is the smaller half of the story.
B a reported missing trial was checked and the exclusion is correctA cross-lane check reported that this pool carries three of four trials and that the omitted one is the only one favouring the drug. The fourth registration is NCT00230971, and its comparator is ceftriaxone plus metronidazole, not imipenem/cilastatin. Adding it would combine two comparators in one estimate. The exclusion stands; it is now recorded, which it was not before.
C the house sensitivity interval already includes no differenceThis object's own sensitivity analyses are the place to read this estimate against. Changing the summary statistic to an odds ratio gives 0.4987 (0.1955 to 1.2722) and reversing which category counts as the event gives 1.8683 (0.7784 to 4.4844) -- both include no difference. An inferiority reading taken from 0.9351 (0.8885 to 0.9842) does not survive this object's own robustness checks, and that is recorded here rather than left for a reader to assemble.
Access limitationBoth syntheses are open access and both full texts were retrieved from PubMed Central and read, so the statements below are taken from methods sections and reference lists rather than from abstracts. An earlier version of this block said neither full text was retrievable. That was false, and it was false in the worst way available: no attempt had been made, while the PMC identifier for each sat in this object's own staged PubMed record. A reviewer read the staged record and found them. What remains genuinely unresolved is narrower and is stated below.
Why this is not an adjudicated disputeA blind second assessor from a different model family disagreed with this domain on 89% of judgements across 22 topics. That would ordinarily be a dispute to adjudicate. It is not one: the tool's own text names this exact evidential situation -- a bare statement that a study was randomised -- and prescribes the answer. The second assessor is not being deferred to; the guidance is being applied.
What the registry gives and does notA ClinicalTrials.gov design module records `allocation: Randomized`. It carries no sequence-generation method and no allocation-concealment mechanism. The original judgement's own note said so before scoring LOW.
How this maps to the tool s algorithmThe tool maps 'No information' on 1.1 and 1.2 with no baseline concern to a domain judgement of some concerns. This project writes no information on the domain when it could not be judged from the sources read, and caps the overall at some concerns. Same place, and it keeps 'we could not judge this' distinguishable from 'we judged it and had concerns'.
What does not changeNo overall rating and no GRADE CERTAINTY moves. All 51 judgements were already capped at some concerns or HIGH by another no information domain.
And it bounds a finding of oursClass 94 records assessor 2 saying no information on the randomisation process/deviations from the intended intervention/missing outcome data `100 of 100`. Measured across all 23 topics now stored that is 239 of 243, and all four exceptions are the randomisation process=some concerns on `agyw-hiv-prep-review` and `cab-prep-hiv-review` -- two of the three topics asked under the earlier prompt build, the one whose reply ids are bare NCTs. Under that build it is 4 of 6; under the later build 0 of 75. The 100% was measured on the later build's topics. The two-defaults mechanism stands; its universality does not, and what varies with it is the prompt.
The rate is still conditional on the same allow listBoth numbers are conditional on the fact list in THE_ALLOW_LIST_THE_RATE_IS_CONDITIONAL_ON above. Neither is a rate of agreement between assessors in general.

Each statement below cites the record it came from; those sources are listed at the end of every section. Where the record holds nothing, the section says so by name rather than being left out, so a procedure that was not carried out can be told from one that simply was never mentioned.

Title and review question

Tigecycline versus imipenem/cilastatin for complicated intra-abdominal infection: clinical cure at test-of-cure1

Among trials randomising adults with complicated intra-abdominal infection to tigecycline or to imipenem/cilastatin, how does the proportion cured at the test-of-cure visit compare, and does that comparison survive the choices made in reaching it?2

Sources for this section (2)
  1. title
  2. question

Abstract

Question. Among trials randomising adults with complicated intra-abdominal infection to tigecycline or to imipenem/cilastatin, how does the proportion cured at the test-of-cure visit compare, and does that comparison survive the choices made in reaching it?1

Methods. estimates were pooled under a random-effects model with the REML estimator; risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 (Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials); and certainty was rated with GRADE, following the Cochrane Handbook chapter 14. Randomised evidence starts HIGH and is rated down with reasons.2

Results. Clinical cure at the test-of-cure visit: risk ratio 0.935 (0.888 to 0.984) across 3 trials; 1 of these pooled outcome(s) carries a stated qualification -- a referral or a recorded finding -- given in full in Results and not reproduced here; the trials agreed closely (I-squared 7.3%); and certainty of the evidence was very low.3

Introduction

1Background. This review asks: Among trials randomising adults with complicated intra-abdominal infection to tigecycline or to imipenem/cilastatin, how does the proportion cured at the test-of-cure visit compare, and does that comparison survive the choices made in reaching it? It pools 3 randomised trials, against imipenem/cilastatin. The outcome pooled is Clinical cure at the test-of-cure visit.

[Draft] The evidence identified on this question is 3 randomised trials (NCT00081744, NCT00136201, NCT01721408), pooled here at 0.935 (95% CI 0.888 to 0.984) for cure_toc_me. Certainty in that estimate is rated VERY_LOW, rated down for risk of bias, inconsistency and indirectness. Which of those unresolved points makes the question worth asking now is the author's judgement.2

[Draft] A search for published syntheses matched 22 record(s); 22 were read and 1 appraised against this review. The appraised synthesis is Carbapenems vs tigecycline for the treatment of complicated intra-abdominal infections: A Bayesian network meta-analysis (Medicine, 2019). Whether those differences warrant a new synthesis rather than citing the existing one is the author's judgement.3

Primary trials. No bibliographic search for primary trials was run. The 3 included trials were identified by reading named registrations on the dates recorded on each entry. Published syntheses. It matched 22 record(s), of which 22 were retrieved and 22 read; 1 appraised.1

Methods — synthesis

For clinical cure at the test-of-cure visit, a random model was fitted with the REML estimator.1

Intervals are 95% confidence intervals.2

Methodological decisions follow Higgins JPT, Thomas J, Chandler J, Cumpston M, Li T, Page MJ, et al (editors). Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions version 6.5.1. Cochrane, 2025., version 6.5.1, and the sections relied on are listed in the object rather than cited generically.3

Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 (Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials) (), following . 3 result-level assessments were made.4

A ceiling applies to every risk-of-bias judgement in this review; it is stated with the assessment itself rather than summarised here.5

Certainty of evidence was rated with GRADE, following the Cochrane Handbook chapter 14. Randomised evidence starts HIGH and is rated down with reasons., following . 0 pooled outcome(s) were rated. No domain is rated UP; these are randomised trials starting HIGH. 1 outcome(s) were not rated because their pool is declined or withdrawn: there is no effect estimate to rate the certainty of, and rating one would be certainty about a number this review refused to publish.6

Results

The pooled risk ratio for clinical cure at the test-of-cure visit was 0.935 (0.888 to 0.984, 95% interval) across 3 trials, against imipenem/cilastatin.1

Noted on this pool. A published network meta-analysis of fifteen studies and 6,745 participants concludes: 'No differences in clinical and microbiological outcomes were observed between different carbapenems and TGC' (Yu et al., Medicine 2019, PMID 31577763). This pool reports rr 0.9351 (0.8885 to 0.9842) on three trials -- an interval that excludes no difference, read as tigecycline being inferior on clinical cure. Read this beside the estimate. This review pools cure rates for tigecycline in complicated intra-abdominal infection and says nothing, anywhere, about all-cause mortality. Tigecycline carries an FDA boxed warning for increased all-cause mortality, and complicated intra-abdominal infection is among the indications it was drawn from. Independently of the label, one of the three pooled registrations posts an asymmetry of its own: NCT01721408 reports serious adverse events in 32 of 232 on tigecycline against 16 of 232 on imipenem/cilastatin, read from its own posted results. A cure-rate estimate for this drug, in this indication, presented without that, is the smaller half of the story. The analysis population is part of the estimand and this pool crosses it. Read from the registrations on 2026-08-21: NCT00081744 registers 'no primary outcome is recorded on this registration' (population: None recorded); NCT00136201 registers 'Clinical response for all microbiologically evaluable and microbiologically modified intent-to-treat subjects' (population: ME and m-mITT); NCT01721408 registers 'Clinical Response at the Test-of-Cure (TOC) Assessment Within the Clinically Evaluable (CE) Population' (population: CE). The populations pooled are CE and ME and m-mITT. A cross-lane check reported that this pool carries three of four trials and that the omitted one is the only one favouring the drug. The fourth registration is NCT00230971, and its comparator is ceftriaxone plus metronidazole, not imipenem/cilastatin. Adding it would combine two comparators in one estimate. The exclusion stands; it is now recorded, which it was not before. The inferiority conclusion does not survive this object's own adjustment. The Hartung-Knapp interval at k = 3 is 0.8327 to 1.0501 on t = 4.3027 with 2 degrees of freedom, and it includes no difference. A reader taking inferiority from this page is reading the unadjusted interval only. A clinically evaluable population excludes protocol violators and indeterminate responses, and microbiologically-defined populations exclude patients without a qualifying pathogen. Those are selected subsets of the modified intent-to-treat population and systematically yield higher cure rates. A cure-rate ratio computed in one is not an estimate of the same quantity as one computed in another, so this pooled value depends on which trial registered which population. One contributing trial is OPEN-LABEL (NCT00136201 registers masking none) on an assessed clinical-response endpoint; one registers no primary outcome at all (NCT00081744, open item O0a) so its result cannot be checked against anything; and the three define their primary in different analysis populations. GRADE certainty is very LOW. This object's own sensitivity analyses are the place to read this estimate against. Changing the summary statistic to an odds ratio gives 0.4987 (0.1955 to 1.2722) and reversing which category counts as the event gives 1.8683 (0.7784 to 4.4844) -- both include no difference. An inferiority reading taken from 0.9351 (0.8885 to 0.9842) does not survive this object's own robustness checks, and that is recorded here rather than left for a reader to assemble. Not that the arithmetic is wrong. Not that the direction would reverse -- that would need the per-population counts and is not established. And not that these are non-inferiority trials: The registrations fetched do not use that word, so the design question is unresolved from the registry rather than assumed. Which twelve studies the network carries that this object does not. The abstract names none and no included-study table was read, so the gap is counted and not identified. Read this before the interval above. The estimate is 0.9351 (0.8885 to 0.9842), which excludes no difference and reads as tigecycline being inferior on clinical cure. This project's own hartung-knapp interval at k = 3 IS 0.8327 to 1.0501, on a t critical value of 4.3027 with 2 degrees of freedom, and it includes no difference. The house rule already requires the adjusted interval to be shown beside the unadjusted one where k is small, because that is the honest width; on this pool the two disagree about the conclusion. Yu et al., Medicine 2019, PMID 31577763, a Bayesian network meta-analysis of fifteen studies and 6,745 participants, concluded: 'No differences in clinical and microbiological outcomes were observed between different carbapenems and TGC.' the adjusted interval and the larger literature agree with each other and not with the unadjusted reading. The stored estimate is not changed. Withdrawing or restating a published number is a content decision. What has been done is to put the adjusted interval and the disagreement where a reader meets the number, because a page that concludes more than its own stated method supports had been passing while pages that refuse honestly are marked incomplete.2

The trials' results were closely consistent with one another: I-squared, the share of the variation between them that is more than chance alone would produce, was 7.29%; the estimated variance of the true effects between trials (tau-squared) was 2.5e-05, the heterogeneity test statistic Q was 2.16, on degrees of freedom 2. tau-squared and I-squared are recorded beside this line, on the measure actually used. They are not the grounds on which that measure was chosen.3

The grounds for pooling are recorded as: Identical across the pooled trials: indication, comparator, outcome definition and analysis population. Not identical, and pooled anyway with the reason recorded against each: blinding, region and trial size. Each difference that could plausibly drive the result has a matching entry in the sensitivity block. Where a later pool on this page rests on the same grounds, they are not restated.4

The full model output for every pooled outcome -- the call, the estimator, the heterogeneity statistics and the back-transformed interval -- is reproduced verbatim as Extended data at the end of this article, so every number above can be checked against the software that produced it.5

Risk of bias in the included results

Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 (Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials). The unit of assessment is a result1

A domain that cannot be judged from the sources read is no information, never LOW. Low-by-default asserts a fact; high-by-default invents a defect.2

A second, independent assessment was obtained from: gpt-5 Codex (openai family), via `codex exec`3

The assessment above was made by: Claude Opus 5 (anthropic family)4

How the second assessor was asked: Blind, from scripts/second_assessor_prompt.py, which assembles the prompt from an ALLOW-LIST of registry-sourced factual fields and refuses to send it if any RoB 2 verdict word appears in the assembled text. The second assessor was not shown this assessment and was not asked whether it agreed. It was given this project's NO_INFORMATION-never-LOW rule so the comparison measures judgement rather than house dialect.5

The disagreement rate, reported as disagreement because agreement between two assessors given the same facts authenticates nothing: 11 of 18 judgements -- 61.1%. Reported as disagreement: agreement between two assessors given the same facts authenticates nothing.6

Where they disagree, by domain: the randomisation process 3 of 3 disagree, deviations from the intended intervention 0 of 3 disagree, missing outcome data 0 of 3 disagree, measurement of the outcome 3 of 3 disagree, selection of the reported result 2 of 3 disagree and overall 3 of 3 disagree.7

That rate was measured before this review's the randomisation process judgements moved. It is left as measured: On 2026-08-21 this review's the randomisation process judgements moved from LOW to no information on the RoB 2 guidance -- the position assessor 2 had taken. The rate above was measured before that and is left exactly as measured: it is a published number, it is the record of what a blind second assessor said, and it is the reason the guidance was re-read. Editing it would delete the evidence that the change was warranted. This is the same computation re-run on the object as it now stands, so both are visible and neither is silently corrected.8

Re-run on the object as it now stands: 8 of 18 judgements -- 44.4%. By domain: the randomisation process 0 of 3 disagree, deviations from the intended intervention 0 of 3 disagree, missing outcome data 0 of 3 disagree, measurement of the outcome 3 of 3 disagree, selection of the reported result 2 of 3 disagree and overall 3 of 3 disagree.9

3 the randomisation process judgement(s) on this topic moved. Any the randomisation process disagreement that remains is one where this assessment said some concerns rather than LOW -- assessor 2 said no information there too, and the guidance applied here speaks to LOW, not to some concerns. So a claim that 'the the randomisation process disagreement is resolved' would be false wherever those two numbers differ, which is why the count is re-run per topic instead of asserted once.10

the randomisation process now agrees with assessor 2 on every compared result.11

Class 94 records assessor 2 saying no information on the randomisation process/deviations from the intended intervention/missing outcome data `100 of 100`. Measured across all 23 topics now stored that is 239 of 243, and all four exceptions are the randomisation process=some concerns on `agyw-hiv-prep-review` and `cab-prep-hiv-review` -- two of the three topics asked under the earlier prompt build, the one whose reply ids are bare NCTs. Under that build it is 4 of 6; under the later build 0 of 75. The 100% was measured on the later build's topics. The two-defaults mechanism stands; its universality does not, and what varies with it is the prompt.12

Certainty of the evidence

Certainty was rated with GRADE, following the Cochrane Handbook chapter 14. Randomised evidence starts HIGH and is rated down with reasons..1

No domain is rated UP; these are randomised trials starting HIGH.2

Very LOW certainty. An open-label trial contributes to a pooled assessed endpoint; one contributing trial registers no primary outcome and so cannot be checked at all; the pool crosses analysis populations; and the inferiority conclusion does not survive the Hartung-Knapp adjustment at k = 3.3

Where a result is rated worse than LOW overall, the domain carrying that judgement is: measurement of the outcome on 3 result(s). The overall rating is the worst domain, so these are the domains that determine it.4

Certainty of the evidence, by outcome, with every rating step5
OutcomeCertaintykStarted atRating steps
clinical cure at the test-of-cure visitVERY_LOW3HIGHrisk of bias -- measurement of the outcome is HIGH: an OPEN-LABEL trial contributes to a pooled assessed clinical-response endpoint, and a second trial does not say who was masked. selection of the reported result is no information because one contributing trial registers no primary outcome at all. Two levels, not one, because a HIGH domain is not the same as several some concerns. (move: HIGH to LOW, down 2 level(s)); inconsistency -- The stored refit gives tau^2 0.000025, Q 2.1564 on 2 df, p = 0.3402, I-squared 1.16%. The three trials agree closely -- which is not reassuring here: agreement between an open-label trial and masked trials does not remove the open-label problem, it only means the estimates are similar. (move: no downgrade); indirectness -- the pool crosses an analysis-population boundary: me/m-mITT with CE, and one trial's population is unknown because it registers no primary. The pooled ratio is assembled across quantities that are not the same quantity. (move: LOW to very LOW, down 1 level(s)); imprecision -- and this is the finding: the unadjusted interval 0.8885 to 0.9842 excludes no difference, but the Hartung-Knapp interval at k = 3, 0.8327 to 1.0501 on t = 4.3027 with 2 df, includes it. The inferiority conclusion does not survive the small-k adjustment. The rating cannot fall below very LOW, so this is recorded as warranting a downgrade the scale cannot express. (move: Very LOW -- already at the floor); publication bias -- k = 3; asymmetry tests have no power (Handbook 13.3.5.4). (move: Not assessable -- no rating applied)

Discussion

[Draft] The pooled RR is 0.935 (95% CI 0.888 to 0.984) over 3 trials. Certainty is rated VERY_LOW. Whether a change of that magnitude is clinically meaningful in this population is the author's judgement: no field on this object records a threshold of importance, and none is assumed here.1

[Draft] Across 3 trials, tau-squared 0; 1 of the 3 trial intervals include no effect and 2 exclude it. Whether that degree of disagreement matters clinically -- whether the trials are answering the same question in the same patients -- is the author's judgement.2

[Draft] This review pools 0.935 (95% CI 0.888 to 0.984) over 3 trials. The appraised synthesis pooled clinical treatment success and microbiological treatment success, plus adverse events and mortality over 6,745 participants. Which trials that synthesis carries: Not read. No included-study list in the abstract, so the twelve studies this object does not carry are counted and not identified. Why the two results differ -- whether by population, outcome definition, model or included set -- is the author's judgement.3

[Draft] The evidence base is 3 trials, assessed for risk of bias as HIGH on 3 result(s). GRADE certainty is VERY_LOW, rated down for risk of bias, inconsistency and indirectness. Whether that is enough to answer the question depends on the decision the answer is for, which is not stated on this object, and is the author's judgement.4

[Draft] primary trials. No bibliographic search for primary trials was run. The 3 included trials were identified by reading named registrations on the dates recorded on each entry. Published syntheses. PubMed E-utilities esearch + esummary, executed 2026-08-21. Query as executed: (tigecycline[tiab]) and ("intra-abdominal"[tiab] OR cIAI[tiab]) and (meta-analysis[pt] OR "systematic review"[pt] OR meta-analysis[tiab] OR "pooled"[tiab]). It matched 22 record(s), of which 22 were retrieved and 22 read; 1 appraised. Whether that is broad enough for the claim this review makes is the author's judgement.5

[Draft] Certainty was rated down for risk of bias, inconsistency and indirectness. What further evidence would change the conclusion is a judgement about a trial nobody has run, and is the author's.6

Comparison with published syntheses

Published syntheses were identified as follows. PubMed E-utilities, executed 2026-08-21. Query, counts and per-record disposition in ssot/tigecycline-ciai/appraisal/the screen of published syntheses.json.1

This review was compared against 1 published synthesis(es); the denominator is stated because a comparison against an unstated number of reviews is not a comparison.2

What this comparison found. A published network meta-analysis of fifteen studies and 6,745 participants concludes: 'No differences in clinical and microbiological outcomes were observed between different carbapenems and TGC' (Yu et al., Medicine 2019, PMID 31577763). This pool reports rr 0.9351 (0.8885 to 0.9842) on three trials -- an interval that excludes no difference, read as tigecycline being inferior on clinical cure. The inferiority conclusion does not survive this object's own adjustment. The Hartung-Knapp interval at k = 3 is 0.8327 to 1.0501 on t = 4.3027 with 2 degrees of freedom, and it includes no difference. A reader taking inferiority from this page is reading the unadjusted interval only. One contributing trial is OPEN-LABEL (NCT00136201 registers masking none) on an assessed clinical-response endpoint; one registers no primary outcome at all (NCT00081744, open item O0a) so its result cannot be checked against anything; and the three define their primary in different analysis populations. GRADE certainty is very LOW. Which twelve studies the network carries that this object does not. The abstract names none and no included-study table was read, so the gap is counted and not identified.3

On what basis their trial set is known: Not read. No included-study list in the abstract, so the twelve studies this object does not carry are counted and not identified.4
